mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong earnings growth (INDPRO > 0.5% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a flattening industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND INDPRO monthly change < 0 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism is not activated during a simultaneous labor market contraction (UNRATE < 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by a simultaneous surge in industrial production (INDPRO > 0.4% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.3% for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism is not activated during a period of rising consumer demand (GDPC1 > 2% YoY growth).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (not in catalog, but using RSAFS as a proxy for bond market liquidity) signals a flight to safety and risk-off sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND RSAFS monthly change < -2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong earnings growth (INDPRO > 0.5% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous rise in mortgage rates (not directly observable, but proxy via FEDFUNDS if available).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month signals a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, indicating underlying structural issues and reduced confidence, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0% AND UNRATE monthly change > 0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism is not activated during a period of falling consumer confidence (not directly observable).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1.5% for three consecutive quarters signals a broad-based demand shortfall, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY).
